title: project.yaml
description: A repo's declaration to the software factory: how it ships, deploys, checks and is watched. The author page is docs/project.md.

apiVersion.description: the file format; `factory/v2`, any other is a broken file

name.description: the repo's directory name; a file whose name is not its directory's is refused

host.description: the host the repo's alerts sit on, a key of config/infra.json's hosts (`macmini`), so its Kuma and HyperDX alerts join that host's incident

deploy.description: how a shipped change is deployed and watched

mode.description: how a shipped change reaches production. `auto`: a push to the default branch deploys (CI, Vercel, RollHook), the Watch asks no `make version`; `make`: the lead runs `make deploy` and `make version` reads the live sha; `agentic`: the lead deploys by its own steps; `none`: nothing deploys, done is merged with CI green

targets.description: where a deploy is verified, one entry per place. Empty: the Watch runs `make verify` when the Makefile has it

name.description: the target's name, shown on the project page (`mini`, `prod`)

host.description: the machine the target runs on (`mini`, `vps`, `homelab`). `mini` makes the weekly hygiene pass judge the repo against the run rules for the mini (`runrules`), which it otherwise does only for a repo with a root `mini-services.yaml`
host.consumer: the hygiene runrules probe (apps/server/src/adapters/hygiene/probes/runrules.ts, read from the raw file)

verify.description: how a deploy is proved: `make verify` (or another `make <target>`) run in the repo, or an http(s) URL the Watch GETs and expects 200 from

hold.description: how long a shipped change is watched before it counts as done (`30m`, `2h`, `1d`, at most 7d). Give an asynchronous deploy (CI, a rolling swap) its time here

paths.description: globs of the paths a deploy carries (`apps/**`, `Makefile`). Empty: every path that is not inert deploys. Set: a ship touching none of them records no deploy and no deployed-version check, as a rewrite built beside the running system must
paths.consumer: the ship gate (apps/server/src/domains/quality/gate.ts) and the Watch

migrations.description: Retired: read by nothing; no gate or brief ever used it. Where migrations live and how they run belongs in the repo's AGENTS.md. Remove it.

probes.description: HTTP probes the Watch runs after every deploy, beside the targets

name.description: the probe's name in the Watch's evidence

expect.description: the HTTP status the probe expects

ship.description: how a change lands: a list of `{ via }` rules; any `via: pr` makes the Watch expect CI

paths.description: Retired: read by nothing; no code ever matched a change against these globs. The factory reads only whether any rule ships `via: pr`. Remove it.

via.description: `pr`: changes land through a pull request, so the Watch expects CI on the head; `push`: straight to the default branch

work.description: `true`: the repo stays a work repo though it has a project.yaml: the read token never sees its words and it hears the owner only. For a repo of another organisation the factory builds in

leads.description: how many leads may work in the repo at once (one more for a fix while the line is stopped). Unset: 64, no cap beyond the host's memory, load and accounts; a value above 64 is clamped with a warning. A lower cap is an exception the file gives its reason for (NL32)

lanes.description: resource classes inside the repo: `{apple: 1}` lets one lead of lane apple run at once; `{apple: {leads: 1, memory: 18GiB}}` also reserves that memory on the host for every running lead of the lane. A lane a row or Issue names and this does not declare is unlimited within `leads`

anyOf.description: how many leads of the lane run at once

leads.description: how many leads of the lane run at once

memory.description: the host memory each running lead of the lane reserves (`18GiB`, at most 1 TiB)

run.description: how long one `factory slot run` of this repo may hold a test slot before it is stopped (at least 1m, at most 6h; unset: 30m)

steps.description: the repo's named steps (`unit`, `layout`): the Makefile target, what each needs and where the factory may run it. A step not named runs on the mini

make.description: the Makefile target that runs the step (`test`); `factory project check` warns when it is missing

needs.description: `linux`, `mac`, `browser`, `apple`, `secrets`, `services`, `git`, `network`: what the step needs of its host. `mac`, `apple`, `secrets` and `services` keep it on the mini

remote.description: `true`: the factory may run the step off the mini, on a Linux step host of its own settings, when that finishes it sooner. The repo's word that the step passes on Ubuntu 24.04 in the step image; the owner still admits the project (`FACTORY_STEP_REMOTE_PROJECTS`), and a step red there but green on the mini loses its place off the mini for a hold that starts at 1 hour and doubles with each repeat, up to 7 days

dockerfile.description: the repo's own image for the step off the mini (a Dockerfile in the repo, built on the step host once per content); unset: the factory's (Ubuntu 24.04, git, make, bun and the PostgreSQL server binaries). Required for `needs: [browser]` off the mini

bun.description: the bun of the step image; unset: the version of the repo's `packageManager` (`bun@1.4.3` in package.json)

carry.description: git-ignored paths the step reads (build output such as `packages/x/dist`): they travel with the tracked and untracked files

budgets.description: what the repo's checks may cost; a day over one is a signal on the repo. A key left out is no budget

fast.description: the most the median of a day's fast-tier check runs may take (`5m`)

peak.description: the most peak memory one check step may take (`4GiB`)

fail.description: the most of a day's check steps that may exit non-zero (`30%`)

checks.description: check tiers: a fast local check and the full gate (CI's when `ci` is true). Unset: the lead runs `make check`

fast.description: what a lead runs locally before each push (`make check-fast`)

ci.description: `true`: CI runs `full` on the pull request head, so the lead runs only `fast` and relies on that run (`make merge-guard` still demands it green)

doctor.description: `make doctor`: a read-only command of seconds that exits 0 when this host can run the project, else non-zero with one line per missing prerequisite and its fix. Red keeps every lead of the repo from being admitted and the hygiene `check` probe from running

hygiene.description: what the weekly hygiene pass runs on the repo

check.description: `false`: the repo's `make check` needs a lab the factory host does not have, so the weekly pass skips its `check` probe (with `reason`)

skip.description: built-in probes the repo opts out of, each with its reason (advisories, links, retired, project, deps, ci, agentsmd, readme, stale, deadcode, cochange, runrules, browser, context)

reason.description: why: a probe is never switched off without one; the pass shows it

probes.description: the repo's own weekly probes, at most 16

name.description: the probe's name; a finding is keyed `probe:<name>`

target.description: the Makefile target the loop runs as `make <target>` in a throwaway checkout; any exit but 0 is a finding

signals.description: which automatic sources the repo listens to; a work repo lists none and hears the owner only

github.description: the repo's GitHub issues and check runs come in as signals

label.description: a GitHub issue with this label is filed as a signal, whoever opened it

checks.description: `true`: a red check run on the default branch is filed as a signal

author.description: every new issue this login opens is filed without the label; set together with `since`

since.description: issues of `author` opened before this are never filed; set together with `author`

launchd.description: LaunchAgent labels on the mini whose crash or failed exit is filed as a signal on this repo

heal.description: alerts that wait for their own recovery before they are filed

grace.description: how long the `down` waits for its `up` before it is filed (at most 1d)

runbook.description: run first, before the grace starts

max.description: how many heals in a row before it is filed anyway

policy.description: standing answers: the first rule whose phrase the question contains and whose answer is one of its options settles a Decision

when.description: a phrase the Decision's question contains

answer.description: the option label the rule takes; it must be one of the options

jobs.description: Retired with the old core; accepted and dropped. Remove it.

ticktick.description: Retired with the old core; accepted and dropped. Remove it.
